Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not put my name on it yet, but I can answer your questions.
Q: That's fine for now. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in Houston, Texas, turning left at an intersection with a green arrow. I'd been driving that route for years.
Q: What happened as you made the turn?
A: I was partway thorugh the turn when a vehicle coming the other way hit the front driver's side of my car. I didn't see
it cmoing until right before impact.
Q: Were you able to stop or swerve before the impact?
A: No. I tried to brake but there wasn't time.
Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?
A: My head hit the side window and the airbag went off. I was dizzy and had a headache right after. I went to the
emergency room that evening.
Q: What symptoms are you still having?
A: Headaches most days, trouble concentrating, and I get tired faster than before. My doctor told me it's a concussion
and I've been limiting screen time and reading.
Q: Has any medical provider given you a restriction on work or driving?
A: Yes, I've been told to take it easy and not drive long distances until I'm cleared.
Q: Did anyone else witness the collision or give you their contact information?
A: The other driver stayed at the scene and a man in a truck stopped. I think he gave a card to the officer, but I don't
have it.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add before we finish?
A: Only that I want my car looked at and my medical bills covered. I'm willing to provide my records.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>
